findings_qualitative.value: SiO and H13CO+ show a ring at systemic velocity around a cavity coincident with the 8.6 GHz source

evidence.quote: the cavity is coincident with a strong and compact radio continuum source observed at 8.6 GHz

claims.hypothesis: Is the outflow a bipolar jet plus an expanding shocked shell?
claims.experiment: SiO moment maps, channel maps and PV diagrams
claims.result: Wings to ±70 km/s, ring at systemic velocity, shell ~24 km/s
claims.finding: Jet along the line of sight with an expanding shocked shell

evidence.quote: We interpret then that the G331.512$-$0.103 source corresponds to a jet almost in the line of sight with an expanding shocked shell surrounding its driving source

claims.experiment: Crossing time from shell size and velocity
claims.result: ~2000 yr (<600 yr for the inner hole)
claims.finding: One of the youngest massive outflows

evidence.quote: The source is one of the youngest examples of massive molecular outflow found associated with a high-mass star.
We consider this high-velocity emission likely to be a molecular “bullet”

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: H13CO+ blue-profile dip could be infall or resolved-out ambient emission

evidence.quote: However, such a dip can also be created by resolving out ambient cloud emission, so further observations would be needed to test this interpretation.

limitations_admitted.value: Continuum may be contaminated by line emission; noise higher in strong lines

evidence.quote: though we cannot rule out some level of contamination by line emission
